findings.issue: Evidence summary references Repomix snapshots of 'main' and 'develop' codebases, but the current working repo matches neither — it is a unified monorepo at ~47 prompts/888 findings that has diverged significantly from both reference snapshots
findings.impact: Reconciliation against stale snapshot references will produce irrelevant or misleading comparisons. The current repo has moved past both reference states.
findings.fix: Generate fresh Repomix/evidence snapshot of the CURRENT repo state before attempting reconciliation. Defer comparison against stale snapshots.

findings.issue: 16 critical checklist items in 00_RECONCILIATION_CHECKLIST are unchecked — no compare audit, no UI/UX audit output, no KAS matrix, no baseline, no guardrails, no priority order, no visual baseline
findings.impact: The reconciliation checklist shows zero items ready. Running reconciliation without these inputs will produce ungrounded recommendations.
findings.fix: Complete all checklist items: produce compare audit summary, fill guardrails/baseline/priority artifacts from current repo state

findings.issue: Pre-reconciliation checklist has no git baseline: no current branch capture, no git status, no restore point branch, no commit hash recorded before starting edits
findings.impact: Without a pre-edit snapshot, any reconciliation edits cannot be cleanly rolled back. Risk of unrecoverable changes.
findings.fix: Run git status, create a restore-point branch (recon-preflight-YYYYMMDD), record current HEAD before any edits

findings.issue: Pre-reconciliation checklist requires build/test baseline before edits, but no lint, typecheck, unit test, integration test, or E2E results have been captured for the current repo state
findings.impact: No baseline pass/fail state recorded. After edits, it will be impossible to tell if failures were pre-existing or introduced.
findings.fix: Run and record: pnpm lint (exit code), pnpm typecheck (exit code), pnpm test -- --run (pass count), E2E test results

findings.issue: 5 approval gate categories (auth, DB migrations, deployment workflows, infra/terraform, API contracts) are listed but none have concrete criteria for what constitutes a 'change' requiring approval
findings.impact: Subjective approval triggers. One reviewer might consider a migration filename change trivial while another flags it as high-risk.
findings.fix: Define concrete criteria per gate: e.g., 'auth: any change to authenticate.ts, routes.ts in auth module, or JWT handling'

findings.issue: Pre-reconciliation checklist item 'Confirm dev/prod environment separation is unchanged' has not been verified — the current repo has documented dev/prod misalignment (Node versions, TF variables, healthchecks)
findings.impact: Reconciliation might amplify existing env drift or create new inconsistencies between dev and prod configurations.
findings.fix: Document current dev vs prod state before reconciliation. Run diff on docker-compose files, Dockerfiles, workflow files

findings.issue: Checklist asks 'Is reconciliation main->current, develop->current, or both?' but no decision has been recorded — the target reconciliation direction is ambiguous
findings.impact: Without a defined direction, reconciliation could attempt to merge in both directions creating conflicts.
findings.fix: Record the target direction. Given current repo is unified, reconciliation should be current->canonical (evidence-based).
